strengths: Addresses an important and realistic problem in text-to-CAD: real-world user prompts are frequently under-specified or internally inconsistent, making one-shot generation prone to failure.

Proposes a well-motivated two-agent framework that decouples proactive requirement auditing from parametric CAD code synthesis, effectively preventing downstream code execution failures and geometric errors.
Develops a rigorous data curation and annotation pipeline that maps CadQuery programs and multi-view renders to concise, human-like prompts with strict checks for data leakage and completeness.

Achieves strong empirical efficiency: fine-tuning lightweight 7B open-source models with only 1.6K coding samples and 6K clarification trajectories outperforms closed-source frontier models (such as Claude Sonnet 4.5) in Chamfer distance and invalidity ratio.
Provides extensive experimental validation, including protocol ablations, cross-model user simulator evaluations, human expert studies, and detailed failure mode analyses.
weaknesses: The synthetic ambiguity generation relies predominantly on structured perturbations (omitted dimensions or conflicting numeric values), which may not fully reflect the diverse and unstructured ambiguities present in human design ideation.

The interaction setup relies on the simplifying assumption that the user can deterministically provide exact metric dimensions upon request, whereas real-world users often lack precise dimensions during early design stages and may require co-creative suggestions.

The two-round interaction policy restricts the agent to an all-at-once questioning strategy; while supported by the ablation study on this benchmark, it may limit flexibility when resolving complex sequential or hierarchical CAD dependencies.

strengths: Well-motivated and original formulation: Introducing proactive clarification to resolve under-specified and conflicting geometric constraints before code generation directly targets a fundamental flaw of existing text-to-CAD systems.

Rigorous data curation pipeline: Inverting the text-to-CAD problem by generating natural language build notes from verified CadQuery scripts and multi-view renders—paired with automated code-leakage filtering, compile-and-Chamfer completeness verification, and human escalation—substantially cleans up issues present in prior datasets like Text2CAD (e.g., problematic scaling operations).

Sample efficiency and strong performance: Supervised fine-tuning of an open-source 7B model (Qwen2.5-7B) on just 1.6K coding examples and ~6K agentic clarification trajectories achieves superior geometric fidelity and validity compared to commercial frontier models (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-4o-mini).

Comprehensive empirical validation: The experimental suite includes standard automated geometric metrics (Chamfer distance, invalidity ratio), out-of-distribution simulator testing (Claude 4.5 Haiku), human-in-the-loop evaluation with real annotators/experts, and insightful interaction protocol ablations (Appendix K).
weaknesses: Simplified interaction and user assumption: The framework reduces clarification to a fixed two-round protocol under the assumption that the user can immediately and accurately provide exact numerical values when queried. In practical CAD workflows, users often do not know exact coordinates or dimensions and require iterative recommendations, visual previews, or tolerance ranges.

Synthetic ambiguity bias: The training trajectories for the clarifying agent rely on rule- and prompt-guided perturbations generated by GPT-5-mini (omitting dimensions or introducing numeric conflicts). While human evaluation is provided on 100 samples, the learned agent may partially overfit to the synthetic stylistic patterns of these injected errors.

Limited geometric complexity: The underlying shapes are restricted to the DeepCAD corpus (predominantly 2.5D sketch-and-extrude prismatic mechanical parts). The feasibility and scaling of proactive clarification for more complex assemblies, complex fillets/chamfers, or freeform boundary representations (B-reps) remain unexplored.
Minor presentation omissions: The abstract ends with an unfinished sentence ('Our code and datasets are made publicly available on'), which should be completed.

strengths: Compelling problem formulation: Rather than relying on standard one-shot code synthesis or brittle post-hoc visual/execution refinement, the paper tackles an important real-world bottleneck in text-to-CAD by proactively identifying missing, vague, or conflicting geometric constraints before code generation.

Rigorous data curation pipeline: The semi-automated pipeline for generating concise, grounded natural-language specifications from CadQuery programs—augmented with multi-view rendering, strict code-leakage filtering, and closed-loop execution verification—effectively eliminates problematic artifacts prevalent in Text2CAD (e.g., redundant scaling transforms and verbosity).

High data efficiency: Training ProCAD-coder on only 1.6K curated samples yields an invalidity ratio of 0.9% and Chamfer distances competitive with or superior to frontier models (Claude Sonnet 4.5) and prior systems trained on >150K examples.

Thorough empirical analysis and ablations: The evaluation covers automated simulators, out-of-distribution user simulators (Claude 4.5 Haiku), interaction protocol ablations (Table 11), granular failure mode analysis, and a human-centered evaluation with CAD experts on 100 samples.
weaknesses: Synthetic ambiguity and idealized user assumption: Ambiguities are synthetically introduced by perturbing specific numerical values or omitting explicit dimensions, and the evaluation relies heavily on the assumption that users can readily supply precise numerical offsets and coordinate vectors upon request (e.g., specific workplane translation vectors). In realistic human-agent workflows, users often express intent via relative, qualitative, or functional constraints rather than exact spatial coordinates.

Scope and complexity of CAD models: The benchmark rests on DeepCAD shapes, which predominantly consist of single or few-feature sketch-extrude/revolve operations with relatively low topological complexity. It remains unclear how well the proactive auditing scales to complex assemblies, freeform surfaces, or highly constrained parametric dependencies.

Simulated baseline comparisons: Because proactive clarification is relatively unstudied in text-to-CAD, all interactive baselines consist of general LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-4o-mini) prompted with identical instructions rather than specialized interactive CAD frameworks, somewhat limiting external baseline diversity.

Reliance on LLM-as-a-judge for core metrics: While validated against a 100-sample human subset with high agreement, key metrics (Efficiency and Resolution) in large-scale experiments are evaluated via GPT-5-mini, which could potentially carry correlated stylistic or structural biases when evaluating clarification trajectories.
